messages.content: I'm preparing a short teaching note for a chat application. Explain in two sentences why an append-only event log differs from a derived context view. Use a concrete chat-history example.

An append-only event log records each individual user action, such as sending or editing a message, maintaining an immutable sequence of events, whereas a derived context view reconstructs the current chat state by processing and aggregating these events on demand. For example, the event log might record "User A sent message 'Hi'", "User B replied 'Hello'", and "User A edited message to 'Hi there'", while the derived view presents the latest chat state as "User A: Hi there" and "User B: Hello", reflecting the current conversation context.
Using your example, give one sentence explaining why rendering that saved log offline should not contact the model again.

Rendering the saved log offline should not contact the model again because it can reconstruct the current chat state solely from the immutable sequence of recorded events, ensuring consistency and avoiding unnecessary network calls.
